default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-218.title: Opening-auction price hold
E-218.hypothesis: The session's first trade is set by the opening auction, where the overnight orders were matched; desks that missed it rest orders back at that price. After price has traded entirely on one side of the open for a while, the first bar that touches it and closes back on the old side shows those orders absorbing the pullback traders, so the move resumes away from the open (a hold, not the colour flip of E-077).

E-219.title: Creep-break fade
E-219.hypothesis: A close beyond the recent high/low made by a bar much narrower than normal for its minute is not an initiative order sweeping the book, just quotes inching past the level; with no aggressive side and the resting liquidity of the range still in place, liquidity providers lean it back inside, so fade it.

E-220.title: Counter-value micro-break fade
E-220.hypothesis: A short-term break upward made while price is clearly below the session VWAP pushes into prices the day's average participant already sold at; the holders of the day's inventory (short below value) add there and the break buyers are a small local push, so fade breaks made against the value side (mirror).

E-221.title: Session break-failure memory fade
E-221.hypothesis: Each session has its own character, set by who is trading it: when most of today's earlier short-term breaks closed back through the broken level within ten minutes, today's book is run by responsive liquidity providers and the breakout traders keep losing; the next break is faded on that evidence alone.

E-222.title: Spent-hour micro-break fade
E-222.hypothesis: When the last 60 minutes already covered far more range than a typical hour, the hour's directional flow and the short-term traders' range expectations are used up; a further short-term break then meets profit-takers and no fresh initiators, so fade it.

E-223.title: Prior-settlement pin micro-break fade
E-223.hypothesis: Yesterday's close/settlement is the zero line of variation margin and of many option and hedge books; dealers hedging near it buy dips and sell rallies, which pins price around it, so short-term breaks made while price sits close to yesterday's close are faded.

E-224.title: New-extreme balance dip buy
E-224.hypothesis: Counting today's bars that set a new session high against those that set a new session low measures who has been initiating all day; when the count is lopsided toward highs, the dips are profit-taking against a persistent buyer, and the first close above the previous high after a lower close resumes the day (mirror).

E-225.title: Multi-day channel edge micro-break fade
E-225.hypothesis: Swing traders rest take-profits and fresh counter orders at the high/low of the last 5-20 sessions; a short-term intraday break reaching that multi-day edge meets their size rather than the thin intraday book, so fade breaks made at or near the multi-session channel edge (mirror at the low).

E-226.title: Steady-participation move follow
E-226.hypothesis: TWAP/POV execution algorithms slice a parent order into evenly sized trades, so a window with unusually uniform per-bar volume (low coefficient of variation) and a larger-than-usual move is the footprint of a scheduled order still being worked, not a burst; follow the move when that steady regime appears.

E-227.title: Fixed-point target cluster fade
E-227.hypothesis: WIN day traders commonly use fixed point targets (150/200/300 points) from their entry near a recent swing low; when price has risen that many points from the window's low, their take-profit sells cluster there and the late buyers meet them, so fade the bar where the run first reaches the distance (mirror).
